datasets.label: Derived corona · Dec 2017
datasets.title: HD 35296’s corona, derived from its magnetic field of Dec 2017
datasets.description: No telescope has imaged this corona, and this is not a published result: it is derived here from the star's magnetic map by a standard method. The map of the star's surface magnetic field from Dec 2017 (Willamo et al. · HARPSpol) is continued outward as a field with no electric currents, out to 2.5 stellar radii, where the wind is taken to pull it straight. Gas at rest fills a sheet about the line where that field reverses, as the Sun's bright streamers do; the wind fills the rest. How much gas there is follows from three numbers. The star's X-ray output is measured (Freund et al. (2022), A&A 664, A105). Its coronal temperature, 5.6 million kelvin, is not measured: it is the temperature stars of this X-ray output have (Johnstone & Güdel (2015), A&A 578, A129). Its mass loss, 45 times the Sun's, is not measured either: it is what the X-ray output suggests (Wood et al. (2021), ApJ 915, 37). Stars with a measured wind lie within a factor of 5 of that relation, and one is 38 times below it. It is shown the way coronagraph pictures are: at each distance from the star brightness is proportional to the density there, and only the steep fall-off with distance is compressed. The method was tested on the one star with a published simulation of its corona, ε Eridani, where its density is within a factor of two of the simulation's on average, and on the Sun, whose corona is measured dense along the same line. The rotation axis is 65° from the line of sight, as the map was fitted, and the corona is drawn in the same frame as the star's own maps; where the axis points on the sky and the star's rotation phase today are conventions.
datasets.summary: Derived here, not an image: gas placed by the magnetic field mapped in Dec 2017.

facts.label: Kind
facts.value: Derived here from an observed magnetic map; not an observation and not a published result

facts.label: Magnetic map
facts.value: Dec 2017, mean strength 10.1 gauss (Willamo et al. · HARPSpol)

facts.label: X-ray output
facts.value: 2.7 × 10^29 erg per second, 0.1 to 2.4 keV (ROSAT) (Freund et al. (2022), A&A 664, A105)

facts.label: Temperature
facts.value: 5.6 million kelvin, not measured: the temperature stars of this X-ray output have (Johnstone & Güdel (2015), A&A 578, A129)

facts.label: Mass loss
facts.value: 45 times the Sun's, not measured: what the X-ray output suggests (Wood et al. (2021), ApJ 915, 37), uncertain by a factor of 5 or more

facts.label: Density at 2 radii
facts.value: 3.2 × 10^6 electrons per cm³ away from the sheet, 72 times that on it

facts.label: Orientation
facts.value: Rotation axis 65° from the line of sight, as the map was fitted; its direction on the sky and the rotation phase are conventions

facts.label: Brightness
facts.value: Proportional to density at each distance; the gas on the sheet is fully bright. The fall-off with distance is compressed (log₁₀ density, 1.0 × 10^5 to 1.0 × 10^9 cm⁻³)
